articles.title: Senate passes bipartisan bill to make data centers pay for their energy use
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Senate approved bipartisan legislation Thursday aimed at speeding up permitting reviews to build power plants, transmission lines and other energy infrastructure as lawmakers seek to increase the nation’s energy supplies to meet surging demand and lower electricity prices. The legislation’s sweeping changes would shorten the timeline to start big energy projects and make sure data centers pay for the energy they use. Anger over data centers and rising electricity prices helped usher in a wave of Democrats pledging to clamp down on the energy-hungry behemoths. The 62-33 vote is the first major action by Congress since midterm elections that soundly repudiated President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans. The bill now goes to the House, which approved a more limited, industry-friendly version last year. The Senate bill would overhaul several environmental laws to make it easier to build energy infrastructure, drawing criticism from Democrats and environmental groups about limits on judicial review and changes to bedrock laws such as the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act. Trump urged approval of the bill, calling it a “BIG WIN for U.S. ENERGY INDEPENDENCE and DOMINANCE” in a recent social media post. The bill, formally known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, will ensure the U.S. can build pipelines, mines and power plants more quickly, “lowering Energy Costs for American Families,” Trump wrote. Fifteen Democrats, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, voted for the bill. Two Republicans, Josh Hawley of Missouri and Mike Rounds of South Dakota, voted no. Industry groups back bill, but environmentalists fear it would weaken safeguards Major industry groups representing developers in clean energy and the oil and gas sector support the bill as a way to deliver more electricity to the grid and avoid delays for infrastructure projects that can stretch a decade or more. However, many environmental organizations have denounced the measure , saying it would lock in fossil fuel development, weaken environmental safeguards and make it harder for communities to challenge energy project approvals. “Make no mistake: This backroom deal will pave the way for even more fossil fuel projects like gas power plants for data centers, oil and gas pipelines and (liquefied natural gas) terminals while sacrificing fundamental and common-sense public health and environmental protections for communities across the U.S.,” said Jen Duggan, executive director of the Environmental Integrity Project. Benefits for renewable energy are outweighed by likely increases in greenhouse gas emissions and air and water pollution from the fossil fuel industry, Duggan and other critics said. She called the bill “a gift to some of the biggest polluters in America” and complained that it was being rushed through a lame-duck Congress without public hearings or sufficient debate. Democrats push for amendments A final vote on the measure was held up this week as Oregon's two Democratic senators pushed to add amendments, including one to ban data centers on public lands. Sens. Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden are among several Democrats in both chambers who say the party should use its stronger position in the next Congress to pass legislation that boosts clean energy, such as solar and wind power, while limiting expansion of oil, natural gas and other fossil fuels. “Getting more renewable electrons where they are needed doesn’t tackle climate change if you simultaneously promote the burning of more fossil fuels. Unfortunately, this bill does exactly that,” Merkley said. Majority Republicans stymied Merkley's effort to ensure votes on a host of amendments, including one that would block the Trump administration from continuing to cancel clean energy grants and other Democratic priorities for “purely political purposes.” The bill's sponsors reneged on promises of “a robust amendment process," he said. In the end, the measure was approved without amendments offered by rank-and-file senators. “I do think that this bill is very consequential to the future of this planet,” Merkley said. Major environmental groups, including the Sierra Club and National Wildlife Federation, oppose the bill, citing concerns about limits on judicial review and changes to the National Environmental Policy Act and other laws. The environmental policy law, known as NEPA, requires agencies to consider a project’s possible impacts and allows the public to be heard before a project is approved. The current review process often takes five years or more, and shortening that time frame is a key goal of the bill. “In America today, it takes too long and costs too much to build,” said Wyoming Sen. John Barrasso, the No. 2 Republican in the Senate. “Energy projects that would help lower prices remain frozen for years” as they await approval by the federal government. “Construction cannot start without first spending years in the regulatory penalty box,” driving up costs and creating uncertainty, Barrasso said. The bill’s four main champions — two Democrats and two Republicans — have released a detailed set of amendments designed to bolster support for the legislation. The four senators, who lead the chamber’s energy and environment panels, negotiated the deal a few weeks before the election. Republican Sens. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia and Mike Lee of Utah and Democratic Sens. Martin Heinrich of New Mexico and Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island say Americans are tired of paying more in utility bills while projects that could lower costs sit stuck in the planning phase for years. “We are going to make it easier to build in America again, and make life more affordable for American families,” Lee said. Co-sponsor calls bill ‘the floor, not the ceiling’ for legislative action on climate Whitehouse, a longtime climate hawk who has been criticized by some allies for supporting the permitting bill, said the measure is “the floor, not the ceiling, of our climate and environmental aspirations,” adding that he hopes “to accomplish big things with our big Democratic majorities” over the next two years. But Democratic Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington state said the bill has been rushed and its impacts are not fully considered. Cantwell, who met Tuesday with tribal, outdoor recreation and conservation leaders, said the bill would undermine tribal nations and weaken protections for the nation’s bodies of water, land and wildlife. “Now is the time to slow this process down, to actually have a formal process” to debate and amend the bill, she said. “Don’t sacrifice the Clean Water Act or hunting or fishing grounds, historic or sacred sites, or protections of tribal sovereignty. We all need new sources of energy and power. But this bill, as it’s currently drafted, is not the answer.” Oneida Nation Vice Chairman Jameson Wilson said the bill threatens the tribe's ability to protect its sacred spaces, ancestors, traditional ceremonies and culture. “Any effort to accelerate development must strengthen, not diminish and erode tribal sovereignty and meaningful consultation,” he said. Former Energy Secretary Jennifer Granholm, who led the agency in the Biden administration, said she understands those concerns, but believes recent changes by bill sponsors strengthen protections for tribal consultation and restore important state authority over water quality. “A bigger Democratic majority can write a stronger bill,” Granholm wrote in a social media post. “But it would still need this president’s signature.” Sen. Alex Padilla, a California Democrat, said he supports and even authored many provisions in the bill, such as streamlining transmission infrastructure. But he voted no because the bill contains provisions he said would “irreparably harm California and the 109 federally recognized tribes who call California home.” He said he cannot sacrifice the rights of tribal governments or California’s environment. ___ Associated Press writer Jennifer McDermott contributed from Providence, Rhode Island. articles.title: Trump's cyber chief is out as U.S. grapples with multiple tech outages
articles.summary: By Courtney Rozen WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross was "fired" from his job, a person close to the White ‌House said on Thursday, days after technology outages disrupted US air travel, banking ‌and national security systems. The ouster comes as US President Donald Trump and his administration face ​mounting scrutiny over their response to the series of disruptions over the past week, including a global outage affecting hundreds of millions of Microsoft users and a nationwide halt to air travel that disrupted more than 18,000 flights. The dismissal of Cairncross dismissal ‌is the administration's first major ⁠personnel move since the outages. Cairncross oversaw cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government. Department of Defense Chief Information Officer ⁠Kirsten Davies will assume the position temporarily, according to the source. "The president fully supported firing Sean Cairncross from his position," said the person, who spoke on condition ​of anonymity. Cairncross ​said  in a statement on Thursday night it ​was the "honor of a lifetime ‌to serve" in Trump's administration. The recent technology disruptions are likely linked to corporate efforts to rapidly patch newly discovered software vulnerabilities in the AI age, cybersecurity experts told Reuters. Advanced AI tools make it easier for companies to uncover weaknesses in their cybersecurity protections. The top US intelligence official said on Wednesday the disruptions were ‌separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical ​changes and not a coordinated or state-sponsored ​attack. Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri ​on Tuesday told reporters in Washington the Trump administration should ‌brief lawmakers on the outages so ​they can “share with ​the American people what’s happening here.” Cairncross was an executive at the Republican National Committee before assuming the cyber director role. His successor will need ​to be confirmed by ‌the US Senate, which will be controlled by Democrats beginning in ​January. (Reporting by Courtney Rozen and Kanishka Singh in Washington; Editing by ​Caitlin Webber, John Mair and Lincoln Feast.) articles.title: DOJ ditches lawsuit that sought to pause certification of Alaska's U.S. Senate election
articles.summary: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche appears at his confirmation hearing in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee on Capitol Hill in early 2026. (Photo by Eric Lee/Getty Images) Attorneys representing the U.S. Department of Justice told the federal 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday that they are no longer pursuing a lawsuit against the Alaska Division of Elections over its handling of the state’s U.S. Senate election. In a new filing , attorneys for the federal agency said “this case has become moot,” a statement signaling they will not oppose the state certifying Democratic candidate Mary Peltola as the winner of the election. On Wednesday, Alaska Division of Elections Director Carol Beecher said she intends to certify the election , including Peltola’s victory over incumbent Republican U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan, next week. According to preliminary results through Wednesday, Peltola’s margin over Sullivan is greater than the number of first-choice votes cast for Sullivan and all other candidates combined. When seated in Congress, she will join a 56-person Democratic Senate majority elected amid a nationwide surge of support for Democratic candidates. Last month, the federal government, at the urging of President Donald Trump, sued the state and asked a federal judge to issue an order that would preclude elections officials from certifying Peltola as the election winner while it investigated whether the presence of independent candidate Dan J. Sullivan confused Alaska voters. Trump administration sues to block Alaska’s US Senate election result if Peltola wins U.S. District Court Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the suit , saying the federal government lacked standing, but the Department of Justice appealed to the 9th Circuit. The League of Women Voters of Alaska and the national organization Common Cause, arguing on the appeal, asked the appellate court to issue a summary order upholding Gleason’s decision and asked the appellate judges to punish the federal attorneys that filed the case. “The legal theory advanced by the United States here is embarrassing and indefensible,” wrote attorneys from the American Civil Liberties Union, which represented the two groups. “The Court should summarily affirm and then order the attorneys for the United States to explain why they or their client should not be sanctioned for pursuing a frivolous appeal.” On Thursday, the federal government responded, saying that instead of summarily upholding Gleason’s decision, the appeals court should vacate it, erasing it from the books entirely, because it is now moot. Alaskans have now voted, the federal government said, and ballots for Dan J. Sullivan are mixed with other ballots, making it impossible to determine who voted for Dan J. Sullivan. “The United States therefore reluctantly acknowledges that there no longer exists any means of determin[ing] whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan,” the federal attorneys wrote. In late October, the New York Times reported that Dan J. Sullivan had been recruited by Democratic campaigners who sought to spoil the re-election campaign of Sen. Dan Sullivan. “The purpose of this lawsuit,” federal attorneys wrote, “was always to make sure that voters had the opportunity to cast a vote accurately reflecting their choice of candidate, notwithstanding the confusion caused (and intended to be caused) by Daniel J. Sullivan’s campaign, egged on by Peltola’s.” While the civil lawsuit is winding down, a separate criminal investigation is continuing. The Anchorage Daily News reported on Wednesday that both the Alaska Bureau of Investigation and FBI are continuing to investigate whether any laws were violated by Dan J. Sullivan’s recruitment as a candidate. SUBSCRIBE: GET THE MORNING HEADLINES DELIVERED TO YOUR INBOX. articles.title: California State Bar opens investigation into former White House press secretary
articles.summary: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, right, joins President Trump as he departs on the South Lawn of the White House on Oct. 13. (Chip Somodevilla / Getty Images) The State Bar of California has opened an investigation into Katie Zacharia, who faced scrutiny during her brief stint as White House press secretary for calling herself a lawyer despite never passing a bar exam. The probe, which was made public on Thursday, comes in response to a complaint submitted last month by the nonprofit watchdog Campaign for Accountability alleging that Zacharia may have violated California law by touting herself as lawyer. While Zacharia, a Huntington Beach native, received a law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, she did not pass the bar exam in California or any other state. Yet, since at least early 2025 she has described herself as a lawyer on national television and in podcasts, including on “The Greg Kelly Show” and CNN, and has been identified on screen as a lawyer in at least 18 appearances on Fox News, according to the complaint. “Ms. Zacharia has represented herself as a lawyer repeatedly to buttress her reputation and credibility as a television legal commentator and now as the White House spokesperson, yet it seems it was all a lie. In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime,” the organization’s executive director Michelle Kuppersmith said in a news release last month. Read more: Questions swirl about new White House press secretary's resume The watchdog’s complaint alleges Zacharia claimed to have served as “outside counsel” to the World Bank and the International Finance Corporation, and previously listed herself on LinkedIn as full-time General Counsel of Fix California, a nonprofit. A spokesperson for Zacharia denied that she had violated any laws in a text message to The Times, calling the accusations “baseless.” “This complaint is politically motivated and a clear waste of the State Bar’s time and resources. We are confident it will be dismissed with no finding of wrongdoing,” the spokesperson said. Under California state law a person presenting themselves as being entitled to practice law without an active state bar license could be charged with a misdemeanor and face up to a year in county jail and a $1,000 fine. Read more: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is leaving the job after a rocky start Zacharia addressed the scrutiny last month in an interview with conservative outlet Human Events, saying she had been preparing to take the bar exam in California shortly after getting married and was busy preparing for a move to China to join her new husband, who had been working in private equity in Beijing. “I was obviously incredibly distracted and overwhelmed and excited for finally being married to someone who I’d been long distance from for at least a year,” Zacharia told the outlet, adding that the results of the exam were “somewhat inconsequential” because she knew she would not need the credential in China. She said she had consulted several legal experts to ensure the title of lawyer was accurate when offering legal analysis and “they said absolutely, absolutely across the board. You can call yourself a lawyer,” she told the outlet. Zacharia added that it was “unfortunate that people dub this as some kind of conspiracy.” Times staff writer Clara Harter contributed to this report. articles.title: Trump's energy deal with Putin and Xi isn't sitting well with some Republicans
articles.summary: Ukraine’s allies in Congress and across Europe were despondent Thursday, fearing that President Donald Trump’s latest gambit to increase global fuel supplies will weaken their effort to stop Russia’s aggression. Their concern followed a trilateral meeting in which Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese leader Xi Jinping agreed to resolutions that included increasing energy output and condemning the International Criminal Court and “and other similar bodies” that have tried to hold Russia accountable for what United Nations investigators declared last month to be war crimes in Ukraine. Republicans in Congress called it a “big mistake” that won’t reduce fuel prices. “They use the proceeds of their exports to fund the war to kill Ukrainian civilians,” said Texas GOP Sen. John Cornyn , who is leaving the Senate after losing his primary in May. “I think that's a big mistake, and, also, I think it's the wrong cure for the disease because it really wasn't able to really have an impact on diesel prices before the midterms.” The White House says Trump’s intention is to help end the grinding war in Ukraine, but his critics in Congress and elsewhere see the agreement as empowering the Russian leader, who he called a “friend” at their summit in China and has frequently praised as a “genius.” Oleksandr Merezhko, a member of the Ukrainian parliament, described the meeting as “problematic” and said the optics were “unfortunate.” “Putin comes out ahead here, but only in terms of propaganda — there are no tangible results whatsoever,” Merezhko said. In Congress, multiple Republicans denounced the meeting, and the four-point joint statement issued by the U.S., China and Russia after the summit Thursday in Shenzhen. Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), a frequent Trump critic, said he hopes the incoming Democrats will hold the administration accountable in ways his own party didn’t. “If anybody is going to change it, it’s going to be a Democrat majority that will use leverage and I hope they do use whatever leverage they have to rescind the waivers,” Tillis said, referring to the president’s decision to waive sections of a new law that imposed tariffs on Russian oil and gas. Allowing a surge in Russian fuel products onto the market may end up “disincentivizing the development of refining capacity in the U.S.,” said Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.). White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said Trump is advocating for more oil on the market to lower gas prices and that his dealings with Putin do not detract from his desire to end the war in Ukraine. “President Trump is committed to achieving a lasting, just peace in Ukraine and ending the senseless killing,” she said. “The President has consistently advocated for more oil on the market to lower gas prices for American consumers; he continues to work to end the war in Ukraine while simultaneously putting America first.” Trump’s trilateral meeting came as his special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were in Berlin, meeting with European officials to seek a way to end the war. The president, on his way back to Washington, called into the meeting and said Putin was serious about negotiating a peace deal even as the Russian leader on Thursday denounced Ukraine’s strikes on the Crimean bridge , and vowed retaliation. “We will not negotiate. We will respond to these attacks,” Putin said, promising a response “much more painful” than the damage to the bridge. Still, Kushner and Witkoff, speaking after Trump’s call, insisted that peace was within reach and that the president was pushing toward that end. “The president has adamantly supported a peaceful end to this war,” Witkoff said. “And what I heard from him on the call today, was that he mentioned these very same principles to the other two leaders he was meeting with. He made Ukraine and a peaceful end to this a principle part of that trilateral today and I think needs to be commended for that.” The White House’s readout of the trilateral meeting didn’t mention Ukraine or a peace proposal. Nor did any of the leaders’ statements suggest that Trump pushed for an end to Putin’s aggression against Ukraine or challenged Xi’s role in supporting the conflict through exports of components essential to Moscow’s military. John Erath, who served as National Security Council deputy director for European affairs during the first Trump administration, said the trilateral meeting was aimed at achieving a short-term price dip in world markets with little concern for the broader geopolitical consequences. “Trump understands that an agreement — even a totally paper one — to increase energy supplies is going to have an effect on world markets and probably bring down the price of oil in the short term,” he said. “It’s geared towards the short-term movement in oil prices and what Americans pay at the pump, and I'm not sure there was much thought given for the long-term effects on Ukraine or elsewhere.” Gas prices have fallen significantly in recent weeks. The average price for a gallon of gas is $3.72, down from $4.30 one month ago. That drop is due in part to seasonal fluctuations as well as hopes for a negotiated end to the Iran war. On Thursday, energy markets had little reaction to the news out of the summit. Russia has little capacity to further relieve global energy prices after Ukraine destroyed or damaged 15 of its 35 refineries in recent months. November refinery volumes were cut almost in half, Reuters reported Wednesday , causing domestic fuel shortages and forcing a cut in some exports. U.S. officials have urged Kyiv to spare those refineries but Ukraine — and some of its European allies — have rejected stopping those strikes. Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby visited Brussels last week and admonished Ukraine for hitting oil and gas sites inside Russia, claiming they “have not been effective … nor do they contribute to blunting Russia’s advances on the front line.” NATO allies immediately pushed back with German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius calling Colby’s criticism “quite a stupid thing.” Veronika Melkozerova contributed to this report. articles.title: Former global sensation Fiona the hippo dies after eating a visitor's hat
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Zoo announced Thursday that its famed hippo Fiona has died 11 days after swallowing a knit cap that slipped into her enclosure. She was nine years old. "It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said in a statement. The zoo's animal care team spent days trying to help Fiona pass the obstruction, going so far as to use a vibration plate borrowed from a horse farm to help shake it through her digestive tract. An ultrasound showed bunching in Fiona's intestines; a colonoscopy with a 9-foot scope didn't help, nor did a "giant" enema. “Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible,” said Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike. “We are in shock at the moment. We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore.” It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency. https://t.co/X0GVbDAiEQ pic.twitter.com/7wLF0uclWB — Cincinnati Zoo (@CincinnatiZoo) November 19, 2026 Specialists said surgery wasn't an option for a full-grown Nile hippopotamus. "They have a multichambered stomach for digesting plants — sort of like a cow — but they don't regurgitate and chew cud like a cow does," Jack Kottwitz, an assistant professor at Michigan State University's College of Veterinary Medicine, told the Associated Press . "Those multiple chambers, tissue folds, fluid and digesting food easily 'hide' the hat, making removal with an endoscope from the stomach chambers very difficult." Hippos are also difficult to anesthetize and keep away from water as they heal. Zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley told reporters that Fiona ingested the knit hat on Nov. 8 after it was tossed in the air by a child and flung by a ceiling fan through a 1-foot opening above the viewing windows of her enclosure. “We probably couldn't make that happen again if we tried,” Curley said at the time. “It was clearly an accident." In the days that followed, Fiona’s appetite started to wane. Fiona was no stranger to health struggles; she became a sensation after she was born six weeks premature in 2017. At the time, she couldn't stand on her own and weighed just 29 pounds; the next smallest Nile hippo on record weighed roughly twice as much at birth. No one expected Fiona to survive. Zoo staff had to bottle-feed her with a mixture of formula and her mother's milk. (A hippopotamus had never been hand-milked before.) While teething, Fiona began to refuse the bottle, and clinicians from Cincinnati Children's Hospital were called in to administer fluids intravenously. Fiona in 2020. John Minchillo/AP But eventually Fiona began to thrive. Named after Shrek's love interest, Princess Fiona — zoo staff thought her ears had a similar shape — she went on to star in her own show on YouTube and other platforms. Her plight — and her adorable triumph over adversity — inspired a host of children's books, a line of beer, a bobblehead and even a limited-edition ice cream flavor. She weighed nearly 2,500 pounds when she died. Fiona also became a Cincinnati icon. Her character in the Cincinnati Ballet's 2018 production of Nutcracker reportedly " stole the show "; the same year, a Fiona mural was unveiled downtown. "Our city is heartbroken," Mayor Aftab Pureval wrote on social media, "but we couldn't be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole." “Our hearts are with the staff of the Cincinnati Zoo and everyone who loved her,” added outgoing Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine. “She will be deeply missed.” Amy Acton, Ohio’s incoming governor, said that Fiona’s survival story “brought joy, hope and a little extra magic to our state.” Second Lady Usha Vance, the wife of Vice President JD Vance, shared an undated photo of one of their children gazing at Fiona through the glass of her enclosure. “We are so sad to hear the news about Fiona,” Vance wrote. “Our family loved visiting her at the Cincinnati Zoo.” This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/fiona-the-hippo-dies-after-swallowing-hat-in-freak-accident-at-the-cincinnati-zoo-211146772.html

articles.title: Almost all of Anthropic's employees are now millionaires
articles.summary: Anthropic captured a $1.76 trillion valuation on its first day of trading on the Nasdaq. - Mike Segar/Reuters Anthropic’s stock market debut turned the vast majority of the young startup’s staff into overnight millionaires — some many times over. The company’s headcount stood at 5,300 as of September this year, according to regulatory filings. After Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, about 600 employees entered the rarefied “centi-millionaire” club, with equity holdings valued north of $100 million, according to data from Hill.com , which tracks private-company shares. As many as 2,800 staffers, known internally as “Ants,” have holdings valued above $10 million. And about 5,100 — 96% of the staff — are sitting on equity north of $1 million. “What’s most surprising here is how quickly this this happened,” Andrew Benson, Hill’s founder and CEO, told CNN on Thursday, noting Anthropic has seen very little attrition. “It’s been pretty clear for some time that Anthropic is a rocket ship, and so it definitely discouraged people from leaving because they knew what the opportunity cost of that would be.” It’s not unusual for Silicon Valley startups, which are typically light on cash, to pay their staff with a combination of salary and stock. The promise of a future acquisition or initial public offering tends to keep workers motivated to work hard and stick it out until payday. But few startups have grown as big or as quickly as Anthropic. The company, founded in 2021, had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024. As with most tech startups, Benson noted, “being early is more important, in terms of a financial outcome, than being senior … You could be very low on the totem pole, and if you joined in 2023 or 2024, you’re likely to have a significantly better outcome than a senior person who joined earlier this year.” SpaceX, by contrast, spent more than two decades as a private company before its blockbuster IPO in June. That debut minted around 4,400 millionaires, out of a staff of 22,000. unknown content item - Anthropic’s IPO is also unique for allowing non-founder insiders to cash out on Day One of trading. In most IPOs, staff are subject to a “lockup” period — typically three to six months — during which they can’t sell their shares. But Anthropic’s listing included a complex, staggered lockup schedule that allowed non-founder insiders to cash out up to 10% of their shares as soon as the stock began trading. (It’s not known how many insiders may have taken advantage of the opportunity Thursday.) And unlike SpaceX, which has employees spread across Texas, California and Florida, Anthropic is uniquely concentrated in San Francisco, a city whose entire economy has been reshaped by sudden surges of tech wealth. A rash of newly minted millionaires could soon amplify pressure on San Francisco’s housing market, where home prices are already rising at their fastest pace in years. The typical home there sold for $1.7 million in October, up nearly 19% from a year earlier, according to Redfin. By contrast, the national median home price was roughly flat over the same period, at $416,700, according to the National Association of Realtors. CNN’s Samantha Delouya contributed reporting. articles.title: Judge rules USDA chief's religious emails to 100,000 workers unconstitutional
articles.summary: Religious messages that U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins emailed to the agency's 100,000 employees were unconstitutional, and she must be careful to avoid proselytizing when communicating with workers, a federal judge ruled Thursday. Rollins sent the messages, which included Christian messages and images, from her official email account on holidays such as Independence Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas and Easter. She did not send messages commemorating holidays from other religions. “And so, like the very first disciples to encounter our risen Lord in the Upper Room almost two thousand years ago, this Easter let us too be alive with hope, full of Paschal joy, and confident in the mission each of us has been called for,” Rollins wrote in an April 5 email marking Easter. U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson in San Francisco said the emails violated the First Amendment's establishment clause, pointing to her position of authority, her use of an official email account and the messages suggesting that Christianity is the shared faith of USDA workers. A USDA spokesperson called the ruling “is a completely unprecedented attempt to muzzle a Cabinet Secretary" and said the agency is considering an appeal. Employees cannot realistically opt out of reading emails from their agency director, and the messages could coerce them to hide their own faith or feel pressure to adopt Rollins' Christian faith, Thompson ruled. When disseminating religious messages, Rollins must stop if a colleague asks her to stop, “cannot create a hostile work environment through persistent unwelcome advances” and “cannot use official authority to pressure subordinates,” Thompson ordered. Her commands were quoted directly from a USDA policy on workplace religious expression that Rollins herself adopted. Rollins may discuss her faith with interested colleagues, share why her faith is meaningful to her, politely invite co-workers to religious events and express her views in appropriate conversations, Thompson ruled, again quoting directly from Rollins' policy. Six USDA employees and the National Federation of Federal Employees, a labor union representing 19,000 USDA workers, brought the suit in May. This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/judge-says-agriculture-secretarys-religious-231008901.html

articles.title: California attorney general opens probe into Nvidia over Jensen Huang scandal
articles.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is launching an investigation into Nvidia following revelations of former CEO Jensen Huang’s reported affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials have accused of being a Chinese spy “We’re specifically investigating whether Nvidia’s advanced chips or their confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” Bonta told POLITICO on Thursday. Nvidia's chips are a key component of powerful AI models, making them highly valuable to tech companies jockeying for a leg up in the race to develop new iterations of the technology. Officials in Washington have sought to prevent China from obtaining the company’s most advanced chips through export controls. Bonta told POLITICO an investigative subpoena his office served on Nvidia Thursday is the first step in its investigation into whether the company violated state law, saying other subpoenas might be warranted depending on the information his office receives from the company. “We expect cooperation,” he added. “Doesn’t mean they will, but unless and until they don’t comply, I expect compliance.” Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment. The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this week that the Securities and Exchange Commission has opened its own investigation into Nvidia, probing whether the company’s financial disclosures misled investors. POLITICO has not confirmed the SEC investigation. “There is clear law in California, corporate securities law in California, that makes it very certain that companies cannot mislead their investors, whether it’s in public statements, statements to reporters or statements to the SEC,” Bonta said. Huang has been a regular presence in Washington, using his close relationship with President Donald Trump to lobby against efforts aimed at restricting semiconductor exports to China. Bonta said he is concerned that Huang’s closeness to Trump might cause the administration to go easy on Nvidia. “I’m not convinced [Trump] is going to take appropriate steps here with Mr. Huang,” Bonta said. Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO last week has complicated tech industry lobbyists’ efforts to fend off export controls and emboldened China hawks on Capitol Hill to pursue tighter restrictions on chip sales. Although Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, he has not confirmed widespread allegations he had an affair with Alice Huang while she was an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company that was a major Nvidia customer. The significance of the relationship went far beyond an allegation of infidelity when it was revealed that U.S. officials suspected the Megaspeed exec, who is not related to Huang, of working for the Chinese government. Bonta seemingly previewed his probe Tuesday, when he told Bloomberg that the Huang scandal raised “red flags” about Nvidia’s actions and was “very possibly” something his office would investigate. articles.title: Senate Republicans quash resolution curbing Trump's Iran war powers
articles.summary: By Patricia Zengerle WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - US Senate Republicans on Thursday rejected legislation directing President Donald Trump to end the war in Iran or obtain Congress' approval to continue, backing the president weeks ‌after sweeping defeats in midterm elections largely tied to Americans' frustration with the conflict. The Senate voted 51 ‌to 48, largely along party lines, to defeat a war powers resolution that had previously passed the House of Representatives. The US Constitution says that ​only Congress, not the president, can declare war, and Democrats have argued that Trump may have pulled the country into a long conflict by failing to spell out a clear strategy. Only three Republicans - Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky - voted with Democrats in favor of the resolution. One Democrat, John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, voted with ‌Republicans against it. The vote was the first ⁠on the conflict since Democratic victories in the midterm elections on November 3. Trump's fellow Republicans, who rarely break with the president, stood behind him in support of the US-Israeli war ⁠on Iran that started on February 28. Just 31% of Americans approve of the US war on Iran, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted November 13-16. It was the 21st vote in Congress on a war powers resolution since the war began. Democrats said ​they filed ​the measure to put Republicans on the record as supporting ​the war. SHOWDOWN LOOMS IN 2027 Democrats will control large ‌majorities in the House and Senate next year, and party leaders have pledged to make ending the war a top priority once they take over on January 3, setting the stage for a potential showdown with Trump. Democratic Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia, who has called repeatedly for Congress to take back its control over declarations of war, said the midterm election result reflected Americans' unhappiness about the war, and higher prices for food, fuel and other goods linked to ‌the conflict. "Its unpopularity was made absolutely, manifestly clear in the election ​results of November 3," Kaine said in a speech before the vote ​appealing for yes votes. Democrats made affordability a theme ​of the election campaign. Democrats have also balked at the cost of the foreign conflict, at a ‌time when Republicans have been cutting domestic programs ​like health insurance subsidies and ​free school lunches. Pentagon data in late October showed that the US military had spent over $47 billion to prosecute the war, more than 25% higher than the Defense Department's estimate in July. The latest resolution had passed the ​House in mid-September by 220-204, reflecting lawmakers' ‌growing unhappiness with the months-long conflict weeks before the midterms. A similar measure passed both the Senate and ​House earlier this year, but the Trump administration ignored it, saying it was not legally binding. (Reporting ​by Patricia Zengerle; Editing by Don Durfee and Alistair Bell) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/us-senate-rejects-resolution-curbing-195349892.html

articles.title: 新云的末日？ 黄仁勋离开之后，算力地主们会崩塌吗
articles.summary: 黄仁勋离职，新云板块两日蒸发 12%–25%。 真正被杀掉的是"英伟达隐性信用背书"这一项无形资产：英伟达5305亿美元的承诺与担保簿，才是新云过去两年能以低于真实风险的利率借到钱的根本原因。行业不会破产，破产的是"无长约、无预付款、无投资级对手方"的三无模型；股票的估值体系会从成长股（EV/Sales）切换到杠杆基础设施（EV/EBITDA与DSCR），这个过程尚未结束。 一、发生了什么？新云板块被暴击 黄仁勋离职，市场真正的震中不在英伟达，而在它下游那群"算力地主"。 CoreWeave 从 11 月 11 日的 60.77 美元跌到 53.13 美元，两日累计 -12.6%；Nebius 从 154.69 美元跌到 115.88 美元，两日 -25.1%；IREN 两日 -12.8%；Roundhill 新云 ETF（NCLD）两日 -14.7%。同期英伟达自身只跌了 6.3%。下游跌幅是上游的 2 到 4 倍，这个倍数关系本身就是一份诊断书：市场不是在给"AI 需求"重新定价，而是在给"新云的融资能力"重新定价。 11 月 10 日盘后 CoreWeave 发布三季度财报，11 日股价暴涨 24.71% 至 60.77 美元，成交量 1.65 亿股、换手率 36%，是该股上市以来最放量的一天。12 日，黄仁勋辞职叠加 Nebius 财报，CoreWeave 跌 6.86%；13 日再跌 6.13%，收于 53.13 美元，只比财报前的 48.73 美元只高出 9%。 ETF 的走势比个股更能说明"这是板块性的资产负债表重估"。 单只股票暴跌可以归因于财报、指引或大股东减持，但一篮子股票在两个月里跌去四成、且期间没有一次超过 5% 的反弹，只能归因于对一类商业模式的系统性怀疑。10 月是跌幅最大的一个月，从 23.54 美元跌到 15.23 美元，单月 -35.3%，而这个月并没有任何一家新云出现违约或下调指引——真正的触发因素是 11 月 3 日中期选举后，民主党拿下参众两院，数十项限制数据中心建设的公投案同步通过，以及 10 年期美债收益率突破 5%。 换言之，第一波杀跌来自"政策+利率"，第二波（11 月 12 日至 13 日）才来自"黄仁勋"。 真正的增量信息：租金在涨，而且涨得比成本快 如果只看股价，会以为算力已经过剩。但第三方价格指数给出了完全相反的信号。据 Ornn 成交指数，截至 11 月 10 日的近一个月，H100 租金上涨 16.1%，B200 上涨 34.1%，连 2020 年发布的 A100 都上涨 9.4%。CoreWeave 的口径更直接：7 月对全部 SKU 平均提价约 25%，三季度再提 10%，进入四季度涨幅仍超过成本涨幅；三季度 Ampere 与 Hopper 世代租金环比上涨 30%–50%。Nebius 的三季度股东信写得更细：GPU 小时价格环比上涨超过 20%，每兆瓦年化合约价值（ACV/MW）从二季度的 2,000 万–2,500 万美元升到 2,500 万美元以上，算力预留拍卖的成交价比底价高出 15% 以上，部分实时现货价格甚至高于按需价格。 租金是算力市场唯一无法伪造的现货价格，它比任何一份指引都更接近真实供需。 如果需求真的在塌，最先下跌的应该是现货租金，而不是股票——因为现货市场由边际买家定价，对需求变化最敏感。但事实是：B200 一个月涨 34%，说明最新一代供给极度紧张；A100 涨 9.4%，说明旧卡不但没有报废，还在被推理需求重新定价。CoreWeave 管理层给出的解释是供给端被卡住了：美国部分州不愿批新项目，交付周期拉长，已投运容量反而变成稀缺资产。 把租金曲线和股价曲线放在一起，结论只有一个：市场杀的不是需求，是融资。买方愿意为算力付更高的价格，但债权人不愿意为新云的资产负债表付更低的价格。这 才是理解本轮新云行情的钥匙。 被市场完全忽略的一项，是"旧卡续租"的期权价值。CoreWeave 披露，2027–2028 年到期的存量设备，按当前价格测算对应近 100 亿美元的潜在增量年化收入，且这部分机会尚未计入 1,325 亿美元的在手订单。管理层预计未来三个月收到约 90 亿美元客户预付款与保证金，其中超过 30 亿美元来自"贷款已还清的存量集群续签"。 二、为什么重要？市场真正的担忧 市场到底在怕什么：四张报表同时发出警报 把新云的担忧拆开，会发现它不是一句话，而是四组独立的数字，恰好对应四张报表。 第一张是利润表。CoreWeave 三季度净利息支出 8.46 亿美元，占营收 23.1%。这个比例在 2025 年同期是 22.7%，看上去没恶化，但分母（营收）增长 168% 的同时分子增长 173%，意味着规模效应并没有摊薄财务成本——原因很简单，债务跟着资本开支同步膨胀，资本开支又跟着订单膨胀，这是一个自我放大的循环。D.A. Davidson 分析师 Gil Luria 的判断很直白：数据中心业务产生的收益，尚不足以覆盖不断累积的债务成本。 第二张是现金流量表。三季度资本开支 145.11 亿美元，是当季营收的 3.96 倍；自由现金流 -74.66 亿美元，比二季度的 -57.43 亿美元进一步恶化。调整后 EBITDA 22.56 亿美元虽然创下新高，但只覆盖资本开支的 15.5%。全年资本开支指引 370 亿–390 亿美元，是全年营收指引上限（133 亿美元）的近三倍。 第三张是资产负债表。有息债务 468.73 亿美元，现金 41.22 亿美元，净债务约 427 亿美元；10 月部分无担保债券收益率一度超过 16%，5 年期 CDS 从 10 月 1 日到 11 月 5 日上涨 94%。这意味着债券市场已经在按"准高收益"甚至"困境债"给这家公司定价。管理层对此的回应是"不会在当前收益率水平继续发行无担保债券"，转而依靠客户预付款、以合约资产为抵押的项目融资，以及硬件伙伴的融资。 第四张是表外——也是最容易被忽略的一张。英伟达 2027 财年第二季度财报显示，公司承诺与担保总额达 5,305 亿美元，其中未来采购承诺 3,660 亿美元（主要是 HBM 与先进封装）、租赁担保 1,085 亿美元（含俄亥俄州为 OpenAI 建设的园区 1,050 亿美元）、其他承诺 560 亿美元（含承诺回购新云算力 360 亿美元）。此外还有 990 亿美元股权投资账面价值、250 亿美元未来投资承诺，2026 年以来参与 105 轮初创融资。 这张饼是理解整轮行情的钥匙，也是"黄仁勋离职"为什么如此致命的答案。 新云的商业模式表面上是"买卡—租卡"，但它能成立的隐含前提是：有一家市值 4 万亿美元、现金流 700 亿美元/半年的公司，愿意在背后做三件事——卖给你卡、入股你的公司、承诺买走你卖不掉的算力。第三件事在会计上不叫担保，在信用上等同于担保：它把新云最难卖的那部分"余量风险"从资产负债表上转移走了，从而把债权人的实际风险敞口压低了一个档次。当市场给 CoreWeave 的债券定 16% 的收益率时，它定的其实是"如果英伟达不再兜底，这笔债值多少"。 为什么"换成克雷斯"会被如此激烈地解读？因为在华尔街的记忆里，克雷斯的角色是那个"说不的人"。路透报道，她在黄仁勋离职前数月，曾对 2,500 亿美元俄亥俄州项目的风险提出质疑，此后该担保规模被压缩至 1,050 亿美元；8 月英伟达暂停了与 AI 云厂商的收入分成协议；对新云的兜底也开始要求"有约束力的照付不议合同"，而非此前的意向书。这些动作指向同一条线索：英伟达正在把"战略投资"变成"有抵押的信贷业务"。 站在 2026 年看，空方的"2–3 年寿命论"至少被部分证伪：A100 投产六年后仍能以"有吸引力的价格"签到 2029 年，Hopper 世代租金三季度环比上涨 30%–50%，Ampere 甚至出现"越老越贵"的罕见现象。这说明在供给受限的窗口里，旧卡的残值曲线是平的甚至上翘的，6 年折旧不仅不过分，可能还偏保守。但多方的胜利有一个隐含前提： 算力供给必须持续紧张。 一旦 2028–2029 年 Rubin 世代的产能集中释放、同时推理负载大规模迁移到 TPU 与 Trainium 这类专用芯片，旧卡的租金曲线会从"平台"变成"斜坡"，届时 6 年折旧留下的账面净值就会变成减值。最后结论： 2026–2028 年，6 年折旧是合理的；2029 年之后，它是需要被重新检验的假设。 三、接下去关注？四道闸门和三个日期 宏观变量：利率与政策，谁先松口 未来三个月，宏观层面只有一个真正重要的变量：10 年期美债收益率能否回到 4.5% 以下。如果 10 年期在 5% 以上停留超过一个季度，新云的无担保债发行窗口将实质关闭——CoreWeave 已经明确表示不会在当前收益率水平发无担保债，Nebius 的 2027 年资本开支有 75%–85% 依赖预付款与合约抵押融资，剩下 15%–25% 必须走债市或股权。如果 10 年期回落至 4.5% 以下，二线新云的再融资压力会立刻缓解，估值修复的弹性大于一线；如果 10 年期站上 5.5%，第一层公司也要开始卖资产。 政策层面，需要盯住三个具体节点：一是得州议会在 2027 年 1 月复会后的数据中心立法；二是 PJM 2027/28 年度容量拍卖结果（通常在 12 月公布），它决定电力成本上行幅度；三是联邦层面是否有针对 AI 基础设施的加速审批法案。 产业变量：四道闸门，目前一道都没关 判断新云会不会出问题，不需要预测 AI 需求，只需要监控四道闸门是否关闭。国信证券在《Neocloud 融资深度》中给出的敏感性测试，提供了一个可以直接使用的阈值体系：以 5 年折旧、长约锁价锁量、约 50% 债务挂钩 SOFR、80% 长单 + 20% 散单为基准假设，测算出四个临界点——现货算力价格下行超过 15%，散单项目 IRR 低于 WACC；下行超过 40%，公司整体 IRR 低于 WACC；SOFR 上行 200 个基点，WACC 上升 0.5%、平均 ROIC 下降 0.15%；建设进度延期超过一个季度，长单与公司项目 IRR 均低于 WACC。 结论不会破产的行业，会被重估的股票 回到最初的问题：黄仁勋离开之后，新云世界会崩塌吗？ 第一层，行业不会崩塌。理由不是"AI 需求还在"，而是三个可以被验证的硬事实：现货租金在涨（H100 +16.1%、B200 +34.1%），交付在提前（资本开支下限上调 20 亿美元），旧卡在升值（A100 六年后仍签到 2029 年）。这三件事同时为真，说明算力仍处于供给约束状态，而不是需求坍塌状态。一个需求没有坍塌、价格还在上涨的行业，不会因为某个人辞职而消失。 第二层，估值体系已经崩塌，而且不会再回去。过去两年新云享受的是"科技股估值"——用 EV/Sales 定价，因为市场相信收入会以 100% 以上的速度复合增长。现在市场开始用"杠杆基础设施"定价——用 EV/EBITDA 和 DSCR 定价，因为收入的增速虽然还在，但增长所需的资本已经不能靠无抵押信用支撑。这个切换不是情绪，是会计：当利息支出达到营业利润的 2.3 倍时，任何理性的债权人都要求更高的抵押率，而更高的抵押率意味着更低的股权价值。即便黄仁勋明天回到英伟达，这个切换也不会逆转，因为它的驱动力是利率与债务结构，不是人事。 第三层，会死的是第三层公司。无长约、无预付款、无投资级对手方的纯转租商，会在 2027 年的某个再融资窗口关闭。第一层的 CoreWeave 与 Nebius 不会死，但它们会变成另一种公司：更少的资本开支、更长的合约、更低的估值、更多的回购。第二层的 IREN、Applied Digital 会回到"电力资产"的定价逻辑，成为被并购的对象。 如果用一句话概括这份报告：新云的现金流正在变好，新云的股票正在变便宜，而这两件事是同一个人造成的——因为让现金流变好的供给约束，同时也让成长故事失去了想象力。对投资者而言，真正需要判断的不是"新云会不会破产"，而是"你买的是现金流，还是故事"。前者在 2027 年会得到回报，后者在 2026 年就已经结束了。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: DeepSeek前成员张博开源Linger项目，主打零token费
articles.summary: 11月19日，前DeepSeek-VL项目负责人张博在X宣布开源个人Agent Linger，开发主体是张博创办的SIMPLEX AI TECHNOLOGIES PTE. LTD.（以下简称“Simplex AI”），代码已上传GitHub。 按项目文档，Linger读取本地邮件、日历和文件，操作用户已登录的浏览器；连接外部应用的读取直接执行，发邮件等写入操作才弹出确认卡，用户可随时接管。 权限边界也写进了官方文档。Agent以用户授权的运行环境执行任务，可访问该电脑的文件、已登录应用和命令行。Linger用确认卡和服务端校验限制Agent动作，没有采用沙箱隔离。 按Simplex AI公布的实验室测试数据，在12GB显存加64GB内存的配置下，阿里千问Qwen3.8-Flash-Next的生成速度为45.5 tokens/秒，该速度为模型开始生成后的稳态速度，不含首token等待。零token费是Simplex AI主打的卖点，README与官网均写明本地推理不产生云端账单和token费用。 这组性能数字存在不同测试口径，实际使用效果仍待验证。 让125B模型装进12GB显卡的是PolyStrata，一个MoE推理引擎。文档将其原理描述为分层管理专家权重，部分专家放在显存，其余放在系统内存或SSD，用到时再调度。Qwen3.8-Flash-Next的2-bit量化文件约39GB，这些权重靠分层调度运行，不会一次性载入显存。 官网显示，PolyStrata已适配12个开源模型，包括Qwen、DeepSeek、Gemma、Qwen3.8-Flash-Next、Qwen3.8-27B和Spark-X2.6-4B，另有更多模型在列。发布会用于演示的千问模型只是其中之一，DeepSeek同样在支持列表内。对本地推理用户来说，模型选择不绑定单一厂商，可按硬件条件切换，也不必为某一家模型的云端调用单独订阅。 成本账的重要前提是硬件。45.5 tokens/秒对应的是12GB显卡加64GB内存。 官方另一组硬件规划测试显示，12GB显卡配32GB内存的模拟配置下，同一模型速度为21.3 tokens/秒，首字延迟约3分钟。这组数据来自96GB显卡限制显存预算的模拟，并非真实12GB显卡实测，该档默认推荐模型其实是Qwen3.6-35B-A3B。两项数据分属不同测试，不能直接对照。 8GB显卡档标注的38.1 tokens/秒，脚注同样注明是在96GB显卡上限制到8GB预算测得，不是真实8GB显卡。 官方文档写明，工作数据存放在用户自己运行的服务器与电脑上，但有几类数据会离机。使用远程模型时，模型调用把提示词和上下文发给模型服务商。连接Gmail、Slack等应用、语音识别和实时语音分别调用Composio、Soniox和xAI。后台记忆和Wiki生成用的是Claude Code或Codex等运行时。 Linger的省账限于本地模型推理无需支付token费。硬件、电力和上述外部服务的成本另计。 商业模式上，Linger把本地部署开放给个人使用，同时保留云端托管权。当前不少个人AI助手及Agent产品采用云端模型或托管服务模式，用户通过订阅、用量付费或自备API额度使用；云端模型通常要把任务所需的上下文发给模型服务商。 Linger开源版本可免费在本地使用，另设hosted版本，目前只开放等候名单，未公布定价。截至11月20日，该项目GitHub仓库星标约1.8k。 项目许可证以Apache 2.0为基础增加了商业限制。未经授权，其他企业不得把Linger源码作为托管服务提供给外部用户，也不得删改前端的Logo与版权信息。这一条款把本地使用放开、把第三方托管收紧，商业化空间留给Simplex AI自己的hosted服务。 张博在开源帖中称，如今AI在数据中心训练，再以token的形式租回给用户，智能应该由用户完全拥有。与DeepSeek此前展示的DS-Bot相比，他回应称，DS-Bot的核心是Bot与Bot、Bot与群组的协作，Linger的核心是人与自己的Agent、Agent与本地环境。 张博2019年在香港科技大学取得博士学位，随后进入微软亚洲研究院研究计算机视觉，2023年加入DeepSeek，任DeepSeek-VL项目负责人，离开后在浙江大学任教并创办Simplex AI。 这款产品仍处在开源早期，支撑性能说法的几组数字为企业自测口径，暂无第三方复现。后续值得关注的是，Linger到2026年底的GitHub星标量级，以及有无第三方复现12GB跑125B达45.5 tokens/秒的效果。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 通胀就业双重暴击！12月到底加25还是50bp？
articles.summary: 11月10日，美国劳工统计局（BLS）公布CPI数据显示，10月份美国整体CPI环比上涨0.4%（预期0.30%），核心CPI环比上涨0.30%（预期0.20%）。由于去年10月美国政府停摆导致同比数据缺失，但从环比趋势看，美国通胀并未出现市场此前期待的持续降温。 核心CPI三个月年化增速升至3.75%，创下两年多最大涨幅，六个月年化增速也达到2.69%，潜在价格压力仍然顽固。10月核心PCE环比或将因此升至0.34%（对应同比升至3.3%）。 加之此前公布的强劲非农就业数据，新增就业16.5万，远超市场预期的7万，前两月合计上修8.4万，失业率降至4.14%，平均时薪环比加速至0.37%。通胀粘性叠加就业韧性，美联储货币政策面临较大的紧缩压力，市场对12月加息定价迅速升温。 数据落地前后，美联储官员密集发声。美联储理事沃勒在数据公布前明确警告，若10月核心CPI环比达到0.3%或更高，美联储应在12月会议上严肃考虑加息50个基点，以维护央行抑制通胀的信誉。达拉斯联储主席洛根亦紧随其后表态，认为FOMC至少还需要再加息两次（每次25bp），并暗示冬季加息速度可能快于今年秋季。 此外，堪萨斯城联储主席施密德与美联储理事鲍曼均指出，当前政策利率尚未构成实质性限制，劳动力市场走强与通胀压力持续意味着美联储仍需进一步收紧货币政策。上述表态使12月加息50bp的尾部情形进入市场定价视野。 12月已锁定25bp加息，50bp是尾部期权

articles.title: 日本10月核心CPI加速升至2.2%，加息再添砝码
articles.summary: 日本最新通胀数据显示物价涨势加速，进一步巩固了日本央行（BOJ）下月升息的理由。 日本总务省周五（11月20日）公布的数据显示， 10月剔除生鲜食品的核心CPI同比上涨2.2% ，连续第二个月加速，为今年以来最快升幅，但略低于经济学家预期中值2.3%。与此同时， 整体CPI同比上涨2.3% 。数据公布后，掉期合约隐含日本央行 12月18日加息概率约为86% 。 Sompo Institute Plus高级经济学家Masato Koike表示，此次读数弱于预期，原因包括政府措施及米价大跌等多项临时性因素。他同时预计日本通胀将进一步向3%加速，主要受中东冲突影响，日本央行可能继续对价格上行风险保持警惕。 能源与手机通信费用推高整体物价 分项数据显示，能源是10月通胀的主要推手。 整体能源价格同比上涨2.2% ，扭转了9月的下跌态势。手机通信相关费用涨幅也明显加快， 从9月的10.9%跳升至17.2% ，同样对整体指数形成支撑。 与此同时，政府为抑制公用事业成本而采取的财政措施仍在压低通胀读数，总务省表示相关措施令整体CPI减少了约1个百分点。 剔除生鲜食品的食品价格涨幅放缓至2.2%，其中 米价同比下跌近30% ，为1971年有记录以来最大单月跌幅。一年前，米价还是推动整体通胀的主要因素之一。 服务价格同比上涨1.4%，作为衡量通胀可持续性的关键指标，其走势受到市场密切关注。BOJ同时监测的剔除生鲜食品和能源的核心指标同样录得2.2%。 企业调价计划密集，外部压力持续 在成本端，能源、运输及包装价格上涨——部分源于中东局势及日元持续偏弱——叠加劳动力短缺推动企业加薪，促使企业加快调整定价策略。 据Teikoku Databank数据，日本主要食品及饮料企业计划本月对 1477项商品提价 ，约为一年前的十倍。 Koike指出，当前价格上行压力主要来自外部因素。 “消费支出疲软，国内自生性通胀压力并不强，企业正同时关注需求疲软与来自中东局势的价格压力。” 12月加息预期进一步强化 彭博经济学家Taro Kimura表示，能源成本上升与日元偏弱令通胀持续高于2%目标，此次报告不太可能改变日本央行对潜在通胀已达2%的判断，也不会削弱其对价格上行风险的警惕。 “我们维持12月加息25个基点的预期。” 日本央行此前已明确，其政策目标已从推动潜在通胀向2%靠拢，转变为将其锚定在该水平附近，并于上月表示潜在通胀自2013年设立目标以来首次达标。 周五的数据将为12月日本央行会议的加息决定提供进一步支撑。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 强美元撕裂全球流动性：风险资产何时迎来转机？
articles.summary: 随着美元指数连续四个交易日上涨，一度突破103.50，创年内新高。与此同时，美债市场遭遇抛售，收益率曲线呈现显著的熊平特征：对货币政策最为敏感的2年期美债收益率单周飙升35个基点至4.87%附近，创下两年多来最大单周涨幅；10年期基准美债收益率重返5.15%的高位，距离多年峰值仅一步之遥。 在强美元与高利率双重挤压下，全球主要风险资产与避险品种均未能幸免于流动性抽离的冲击。黄金单周下跌4.7%至约3875.0美元/盎司，为金价自历史高位回落以来的最低点；高贝塔风险资产的去杠杆进程更为剧烈，加密货币市场在周末迎来大规模多头清算，比特币一度下探至62022美元的四个月低点，年内跌幅加深至18.9%。 当前外汇与跨资产市场的定价逻辑围绕美联储政策路径、能源价格波动、AI资本支出可持续性以及地缘政治风险展开。 金融条件实质性收紧，风险资产入场窗口显著后移 10月份美国就业与通胀双超预期 ，市场对美联储12月加息25bp已完全定价，并开始定价12月加息50bp的可能性。自9月议息会议以来，美国金融状况已实质性收紧约20个基点，其紧缩效应主要由美元升值和利率抬升驱动，相当于额外实施了一次小幅加息。 其传导首先体现在融资端。美元持续升值推高非美经济体的美元融资成本与债务偿付压力，美元负债较高的企业和新兴市场国家尤为敏感；长端利率上行则抬升贴现率，压缩风险资产估值，并推高企业再融资与资本开支的边际成本。前期依赖宽松流动性、低融资成本和高估值支撑的资产，在利率预期快速上修后更容易发生估值压缩和杠杆去化。

articles.title: 美元，迎来第四周上涨
articles.summary: 美元正受到多重利好因素共振支撑，有望实现连续第四周上涨。 周四，人工智能实验室Anthropic正式在纳斯达克全球精选市场挂牌交易，上市首日股价即跳涨17%。 这一史上规模最大的科技类公开募股，吸引全球投资者纷纷将本国货币兑换为美元以认购股份，直接推高了市场对美元的需求。 Spectra Markets总裁Brent Donnelly在周四的研报中估计， 此次IPO的海外认购规模约在100亿至150亿美元之间。 与此同时， 美国10年期国债收益率保持在5%以上，创2007年以来最长持续时间纪录，进一步巩固了美元的强势地位。 本周，彭博美元即期指数已累计上涨0.7%，这是自10月9日以来最长的周度连涨周期。彭博美元即期指数今年以来已累计上涨逾3%，对多数主要货币均呈强势。 ICE美元指数亚太时段小幅回调0.11%。 Anthropic IPO制造大规模换汇需求 Anthropic此次上市堪称史上规模最大的科技公司IPO，为美元带来了可观的短期需求。 Brent Donnelly指出， 来自海外的IPO认购规模估计在100亿至150亿美元之间，这些美元买盘集中涌现，与企业在感恩节前完成的常规购汇需求叠加，进一步加剧了美元的供需紧张。 美国财政部数据显示，今年1月至9月，外资流入美国股市规模同比大增43%，达到6700亿美元，为至少2016年以来的最高水平。 Anthropic的上市进一步提升了美国股市对全球资本的吸引力，并有望使其跻身全球最重要的AI概念股行列。 巴克莱、德意志银行和渣打银行均预计美元涨势将延续至2027年 ，核心逻辑在于美国在AI领域的主导地位及其对生产率和利率的潜在提振效应。 高收益率与加息预期形成双重支撑 除IPO需求外，野村证券策略师Dominic Bunning指出，美国国债收益率接近近期高位，令以美元为基础的套息交易持续具有吸引力，进一步支撑了美元的强势表现。 美联储方面，据彭博报道，周三公布的最新会议纪要显示，几乎所有官员均认为，为在合理时间内将通胀压回2%的目标， 央行在"未来数月内"可能需要继续加息。 中东局势的持续紧张则带来了额外的通胀风险，并推升了油价。美国银行策略师Alex Cohen表示： 本周的主旋律是降低风险敞口。美国经济数据和美联储官员释放的信号一致指向进一步加息，且有充分依据，这对美元而言是良好的组合。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 跌破3600，黄金势创3月来最惨一周
articles.summary: 黄金连跌五日，本周跌幅逼近9%，创下2026年3月以来最大单周跌幅。美联储鹰派信号持续强化、科技股抛售潮蔓延，以及美元走强三重压力叠加，令这一曾在今年1月触及历史高点的贵金属陷入深度调整。 现货黄金周五亚市盘中跌幅一度逼近3%，最低触及3520美元，较1月28日创下的历史高点5589.38美元已累计下跌逾三分之一。 白银同期跌幅更深，本周累计下挫约14%。 美联储加息预期是本轮下行的核心驱动力。 芝加哥联储主席Austan Goolsbee周四表示，为应对顽固通胀，他将考虑“所有选项”，成为近期多位央行官员中最新一位暗示加息的声音。摩根大通本周三成为最新一家预测美联储将在 12月、1月和3月连续加息 的大行。10年期美国国债收益率本周已连续逾29个交易日站上5%，创2007年以来最长纪录，美元指数同期上涨约0.7%。 多家华尔街大行对黄金的短期前景保持谨慎，但中长期分歧明显。 高盛将2027年底目标价下调至4650美元，并将当前局面类比为“2022年重演”；瑞银则逆势将黄金评级上调至“具吸引力”，维持2027年底5000美元目标价，认为当前价位的买入逻辑正在增强。 三重压力击穿3600，技术面支撑告急 美联储鹰派信号持续强化。 美联储理事Christopher Waller本周表示，可能需要加息50个基点以“震慑市场”，这一措辞进一步打压市场情绪。 全球投资者目前普遍押注，包括美联储、欧洲央行和英格兰银行在内的主要央行，将在2027年底结束加息后维持利率数年不变。 与此同时， 全球科技股的持续下跌也加剧了黄金的抛压。 全球股市正面临逾三年来最长连跌走势，投资者被迫出售黄金以弥补科技股仓位损失。 高利率环境直接抬高了持有黄金这一无息资产的机会成本。 据CNBC报道，理财顾问Evan Mills指出，货币市场基金目前可提供4%至5%的收益率，“现金在这种环境下表现良好，股票、债券等传统资产组合也变得更具吸引力，人们开始重新审视持有黄金的机会成本”。 从技术面看，Global X ETFs策略师Justin Lin表示，黄金“目前已明确进入真空地带，在3300至3400美元区域之前几乎没有技术支撑”，并称该金属“目前看起来非常脆弱，我很难看到什么因素能在短期内扭转势头”。 据CNBC报道，Bannockburn Capital Markets首席市场策略师Marc Chandler认为金价将下探3500至3600美元区间，并警告称“图表上没有任何信号显示底部已经形成”，建议投资者“耐心等待出现反转形态”。 从历史高点到深度回调：黄金角色之变 黄金在2025年创下53次历史新高，并于今年1月28日触及5589.38美元的历史峰值，此后展开大幅回调。渣打银行全球大宗商品研究主管Suki Cooper将此次下跌归因于黄金所扮演角色的转变——从“投资组合避险资产”变为“流动性提供者”。 Cooper解释称，中东冲突爆发后，由于黄金流动性强、易于变现，投资者开始出售黄金以筹集现金，引发了第一轮调整。 高盛对此提供了理论框架： 通胀冲击可分为两类，一是机构公信力受损引发的货币信用危机（如上世纪70年代），彼时黄金大幅上涨；二是供给侧冲击（如本次霍尔木兹危机），此类情景下被扰动的大宗商品本身表现更优，而黄金往往因货币政策收紧引发的保证金补缴抛售而“阶段性跑输”。 高盛的结论是： 黄金在美联储失去公信力时胜出，在美联储被迫证明其公信力时落败。 据CNBC报道，美国铸币局前局长、美国货币储备公司总裁Philip Diehl表示，推动黄金牛市的基本面依然存在，但美国贸易政策和地缘政治联盟的急剧转变，叠加伊朗战争，构成了对黄金的“黑天鹅”冲击。他预计，随着油价正常化和利率趋稳，“黄金价格将于2027年恢复上行轨迹”。 高盛：2027年像极了2022年，央行买盘是唯一支柱 华尔街见闻文章 写道，高盛大宗商品团队Lina Thomas领衔，本周发布2027年贵金属年度展望，将黄金年底目标价由4800美元再度下调至4650美元，并首次给出2028年底目标价5600美元。 这已是该团队在11天内第二次下调目标价。 高盛将当前局面概括为“2027年像极了2022年”：美联储加息压制西方ETF投资需求，但各国央行持续购金形成坚实托底。高盛经济学家预计，美联储将于12月和明年3月分别再加息25个基点，对利率敏感的西方ETF持仓将持续承压。真正的转机要等到2027年11月至2028年9月间的四次降息，届时政策利率将回落至3.25%至3.5%的终端水平。 高盛还提醒投资者， 不要期待ETF买家会抢先布局 ——据其测算，每降息一次25个基点，仅能带动约60吨ETF需求增量，且这一过程将分散在六个月内逐步兑现。 在下行情景方面，高盛设定了两种压力测试：若美联储加息四次且终端利率更高，2027年底目标价将降至4585美元；极端情形下，若过去三年积累的ETF持仓因利率上升全面平仓，将触发约300吨抛售，届时金价可能低至4265美元。 在央行购金方面，高盛结构性看涨黄金的核心假设是各国央行在2026年至2028年间维持每月约60吨的购金节奏，远高于2022年前每月仅17吨的历史均值。高盛还指出，英格兰银行托管的央行黄金持仓在9月单月激增82吨，暗示存在未被官方数据捕捉的场外交易购金行为， 官方部门实际购金量或超过公开数据所呈现的水平。 瑞银逆势上调评级，但承认等待时间更长 与高盛的谨慎基调不同，瑞银在其2027年度展望报告中逆势将黄金评级上调至“具吸引力”，维持2027年12月底5000美元的目标价，较当前价位意味着约40%的上涨空间。 不过，瑞银也承认通往5000美元的路径正在拉长。 瑞银在8月时预计黄金将于2027年上半年触及5000美元，10月时其首席投资办公室预测为2027年9月前达到5400美元，而本周已将5000美元目标推迟至2027年第四季度。 瑞银的核心逻辑在于实际收益率的最终回落。 该行预计，随着通胀降温，债券收益率将于2027年下半年温和下行，届时将解除对金价上涨的压制。瑞银首席投资办公室预计美联储将于12月和明年3月再度加息，在此之前，央行购金更多是在减缓金价下跌，而非推动反转。 在资产配置层面，瑞银将债券和大宗商品列为最具风险回报吸引力的资产类别，将全球股票下调至中性，现金为最不受青睐的资产。瑞银将大宗商品定位为对冲地缘政治风险、通胀和供应约束的工具，黄金处于这一逻辑的核心位置。 目前主要大行对黄金2027年底的目标价分别为：摩根士丹利5250美元、瑞银5000美元、高盛4650美元，三家机构均预计金价将从当前水平回升，但均不认为在美联储仍处于加息周期期间会出现快速反转。
